title: RDNA 5, PS6 and Xbox Helix versus RTX 5080 and RTX 5090

applicability.context: Rasterization, ray/path tracing, graphics AI and memory; no hardware purchase or installation.

observations.claim: Sony's Amethyst publication describes Neural Arrays, dedicated Radiance Cores and Universal Compression.
Xbox describes a custom AMD SoC and an order-of-magnitude RT advance; no comparative benchmark method is supplied. Alpha hardware is planned for developers in 2027.
AMD describes FSR Diamond with neural rendering, ML upscaling, ML multi-frame generation and Ray Regeneration, optimized for Helix/GDK.
An older direct Kepler estimate places PS6 near RX 9070 XT and Xbox near RTX 5080. This is neither an official specification nor a measured raster benchmark.
September 2026 Kepler posts claim PS6 40 TFLOPS and Helix 56 TFLOPS. PS6's 40 already includes dual issue; the 80 TFLOPS interpretation is rejected.

A 2025 thread quotes Kepler's most-likely memory expectations of PS6 30 GB and Xbox 36 GB. Kepler directly rejected the older 48 GB Helix SKU possibility in September 2026. Final retail capacities remain unconfirmed.
Kepler estimated approximately 1200 TOPS for PS6 in an INT8 discussion. Precision, density and workload are insufficiently defined for a cross-vendor performance ranking.

nvidia_reference_specs.metrics_are: Compute throughput figures are published theoretical peaks at the reference boost clock; bandwidth is nominal, while VRAM capacity and TGP are reference specifications. None of these figures is game FPS.

benchmark_anchors.coverage: Historical published desktop tests, read in October 2026; not a new local benchmark or console test. Each suite matches per-game settings between the compared cards. Raster suites combine native rendering and upscaling at 4K output.

inferences.claim: Under the older desktop-equivalence rumor, PS6 is plausibly below RTX 5080 in raster and Helix near RTX 5080. RTX 5090 would retain a substantial raster-performance lead in this conditional comparison.

The newer 56/40 ratio is 40% more theoretical shader throughput. It cannot be applied equally to raster FPS, RT, AI or entire-system performance, and does not independently validate the older desktop-equivalence estimate.

Large RT/AI improvements from a current-console baseline are compatible with performance below RTX 5090. Exact RT and AI placements remain unknown; RTX 5080-class RT is only an unverified possibility.

Unified console RAM shares capacity with CPU-side game and system data. It has no fixed conversion to dedicated VRAM; compression and shared allocations further complicate the comparison. More capacity alone does not establish more bandwidth or FPS.
A desktop RDNA 5 GPU can use different resources, power and memory than either console. Console estimates do not establish the architecture's desktop performance ceiling.

illustrative_calculation.assumptions: Assume PS6 actually renders at 80% of RTX 5080, Helix actually renders 40% faster in the same workload, and RTX 5090 renders at 150% of RTX 5080.
illustrative_calculation.warning: The second assumption is not proven by the 56/40 TFLOPS claim. Do not merge the earlier equivalence leak and later FLOPS leak into one measured forecast.

rejected_interpretations: PS6 has 80 TFLOPS after adding dual issue again.
40% greater shader throughput guarantees 40% more FPS or AI speed.
An RT hardware multiplier equals the full-frame multiplier.
1200 INT8 TOPS can be ranked directly against 1801 or 3352 sparse FP4 TOPS.
30–36 GB unified memory equals 30–36 GB dedicated VRAM.
Neural rendering as a category proves parity with DLSS 5's specific image-processing method.
Frame-generated display FPS establishes base render speed or simulation rate.

success_evidence: Matched game scenes, settings, internal/output resolution and base/displayed FPS.
RT/PT and neural inference times with common workloads, precision and sparsity definitions.
Published usable memory budgets and bandwidth.

permission.scope: Research and preservation only; no installations, purchases, benchmarks, account setting changes or scheduling.

change_triggers: Original rumor correction affecting these claims.

next_boundary: Replace conditional comparisons when primary specifications or matched measurements exist; no automated monitoring has been activated.
